title: SIU probe fatal shooting; Kitchener man, 26, died with drugs in his hands; only 2nd time in 30 years that police shoot and kill a suspect
article: A man was fleeing with stolen prescription drugs when he was shot and killed Tuesday night by a Waterloo regional police officer.
The death of Trevor Colin Graham, 26, of Kitchener marked just the second time in 30 years that a local officer has killed anyone with a service pistol.

Graham was leaving the Shoppers Drug Mart store in the Sunrise Centre in Kitchener about 9:30 p.m. when two uniformed officers responding to a robbery call met him in the front vestibule between two sets of doors.
There was a brief exchange before one of the officers shot Graham once in the chest.
Frank Phillips, a spokes- person for the provincial Special Investigations Unit, couldn't say if Graham was armed or if there was a struggle before the fatal shooting.
"I don't know that for sure," he said. "We have to find out exactly what led the officer to draw her pistol and fire."
The unit -- an agency that looks into all police incidents in which civilians are killed or seriously injured -- has assigned five investigators and three forensic technicians to the case.
The constable who fired the fatal shot, a five-year police veteran, remains on active, front-line duty.
"There's no reason to suspend her," said regional police Insp. Bryan Larkin. "There's no reason to reassign her."
Witnesses said they saw an officer trying to resuscitate a man lying in the entranceway of the Ottawa Street South store.
Graham was taken away in an ambulance and pronounced dead at Grand River Hospital in Kitchener.
Phillips wouldn't release other details of the shooting, saying an investigation to determine if the officer did anything wrong will likely take four to six weeks.
The same drugstore was held up by an armed, masked man on Nov. 14, part of a rash of robberies in that area of Kitchener in recent weeks.
Just three hours earlier that night, a man wearing a ski mask pointed a gun and demanded drugs and money at a Highland Road pharmacy.
Pat Chapman, a spokesperson for Shoppers Drug Mart, said a security guard was hired after the armed robbery at the Sunrise Centre store last week.
The guard called 911 when Graham came in looking for drugs, she said, and a manager hid employees in a staff room. Chapman didn't know whether Graham was armed.
She said workers have been offered counselling, and an off-duty police officer will be paid to provide security for the next few weeks after the store's scheduled reopening today.
"Obviously, this is difficult and shocking," she said.

A plaza manager says police will have digital video that may link the Nov. 14 robbery at Shoppers to Tuesday's attempted robbery. Steve Voisin, a site manager at the Sunrise shopping plaza who oversees security, said he has reviewed the parking lot surveillance tapes from both nights and believes the crimes were committed by the same person.
The footage he provided police with last week allowed them to get a description of the suspect's vehicle, a dark passenger car. He said that car was visible in the parking lot again Tuesday.

"I think we have his car on video," Voisin said. "I think the police will be able to verify that it was the same guy, compared to last week's video. Once I provide my tape, I'm sure they'll be able to say, 'there's his car again.'"

Voisin planned to hand over about 15 minutes of the surveillance footage -- which he said also shows the suspect entering the drugstore -- by the end of the day yesterday. It was captured by one of the plaza's several dozen security cameras, which cover the parking lot and all store entrances.

A memo will be sent out to all the plaza's tenants, Voisin said, urging them to review their emergency plans in the wake of the shooting. Shoppers had reviewed theirs after last week's robbery, and Voisin feels they were better prepared for a robbery the second time around.
The last time a local officer shot and killed anyone was in 1977, when a constable investigating a domestic dispute fired at Miroslav Milojkovic, 57, on Edwin Street in Kitchener.
A coroner's jury later cleared Const. Fred Barens of any wrongdoing.
On only two other occasions since the formation of Waterloo regional police in 1973 have officers shot and injured anyone.
"It's always regrettable, always tragic, but we still believe we're a very safe community," Larkin said.
Throughout the province, there were 34 fatal police shootings from 2000 to 2006, only one of which resulted in criminal charges.
The investigations unit is asking anyone who was in or near the drugstore around the time of this week's robbery and shooting to come forward.
"I'm sure somebody saw something," Phillips said. "They may have seen this guy skulking around outside."
